## Sheet: Instructions
|  | Introduction to Battery Pass "Data attribute longlist" | As an addendum to the Battery Passport Content Guidance version 1.1, the Battery Pass consortium synthesised the data attribute requirements and definitions in collaboration with the Global Battery Alliance ID working group in this document - the "Data Attribute Longlist version 1.1". 
It can serve as the semantic basis for implementing the battery passport, as the data requirements are mapped out and accordingly described.

|  | EV | Definition of whether data attributes are mandatory for the respective battery categories (EV, LMT, Other Industrial >2 kWh, Stationary >2 kWh). "Other Industrial" comprises all industrial batteries except stationary battery energy storage systems, which are covered by "Stationary". The mandatory requirement follows either from the Battery Regulation (marked with 'x') or other regulations such as the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (marked with '(x)'). |  | Data bahavioural characteristic: static vs. dynamic | Definition of whether a data attribute is static or dynamic. The Battery Pass defines static data as "data, which is provided upon placing the battery on the market and which may only change through its lifetime, if the battery is subject to a replacement of parts or a change to the operational boundaries set by the battery management system" and follows the European Commission definition of dynamic data as "data that change often or on a regular basis”. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  | Pack | Definition of level of granularity in terms of whether the data attribute needs to be reported on 1) battery pack, 2) battery module or 3) battery cell level. (Definitions from Art. 3 Battery Regulation)
1) Battery pack means any set of battery cells that are connected together or encapsulated within an outer casing, so as to form a complete unit which is not meant to be split up or opened by the end-user. 2) Battery module means any set of battery cells that are connected together or encapsulated within an outer casing to protect the cells against external impact, and which is meant to be used either stand-alone or in combination with other modules. 3) Battery cell means the basic functional unit in a battery composed of electrodes, electrolyte, container, terminals and, if applicable, separators and containing the active materials the reaction of which generates electrical energy.

Note on columns S-U in tab "Data attribute longlist": Currently, the Battery Regulation mandates battery passport data reporting on the highest level, which often is the battery pack (industrial, EV batteries) or a stand-alone module (e.g., LMT batteries).
